**Due Sunday October 11, 11:59pm. Closed-book quiz in class Monday October 12 (first 30 minutes).**

15 points: a short study note (5, graded on completion) and the quiz (10).

## The concepts

The quiz covers six concepts from Experimentology Chapters
[5](https://experimentology.io/005-estimation.html),
[6](https://experimentology.io/006-inference.html), and
[10](https://experimentology.io/010-sampling.html):

1. **p-values.** What a p-value is and is not; what the distribution of p-values looks like
   under the null and under a true effect.
2. **Multiplicity.** How the false-positive rate grows with the number of tests.
3. **p-hacking.** Optional stopping, selective reporting of outcomes, and flexible
   exclusions or subgroups; why each inflates false positives, and how preregistration helps.
4. **Statistical power.** Power as a function of effect size, N, and alpha; what
   underpowered studies do to the literature; why pilots cannot estimate effect sizes.
5. **Confidence intervals.** What a confidence interval does and does not tell you.
6. **Bayes factors.** What a Bayes factor compares; how to read BF10 = 3, 10, or 1/3; how it
   differs from a p-value.

## Study however you want

How you learn these is up to you, and using agents is encouraged. Some things you might
do: have an agent build an interactive simulator and then try to break it; ask an agent to
generate practice questions; build a small Quarto tutorial with simulations of optional
stopping. You do not have to build anything.

## What you turn in

One paragraph on what you did to study, with links to anything you created (a repo, a
page, a notebook, a shared chat). That's it. Submit it as text on Canvas.

## The quiz

Paper, 30 minutes, no devices, about 15 questions: short answer, numerical, and
sketching. Several questions ask you to **draw a plot** (a p-value distribution, a power
curve) or to **read a plot** we give you. Bring a pencil.
